sources.note: Identity only: Yellow Yi, <300 speakers (Bradley 2005, 2007), 4 villages in NW Fumin and 1 in NW Anning, migrated from Sichuan, 'most closely related to Suondi Yi according to Bradley (2005)'; Shilin Nyisu (Gaohanshan village, Zhuqing township) documented in Wu 1997 and YNYF 1984; 'It is not known whether Nyisu of Shilin and Nyisu of Kunming are closely related.' Nothing on stress.

sources.note: Nyisu occurs only as a 2003 elicitation point in Table 3.1 (p. 67: 'Nyisupo [ȵi55su33pho21] EY Lu Cuiling 25 06/07 Luomian TW, Fumin CT, YN 富民县罗免乡'); sec. 3.6 (p. 67) says only Gepu, Samu, Lipo, Maang and Azha of those points are used, so no Nyisu inventory or profile is given. The words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in the thesis; sec. 4.4.1 (p. 88) gives only 'tonemes are from 3 to 8' for Nisoic generally. SILENT on Nyisu and on stress.
